CAPABILITIES.visibility: The master reads the master strategy in its fixed system instructions, an overview of every worker's policy at the end of each of its requests, and the full policies with their change logs in a read-only file. Each worker reads its own current policy at the end of each of its requests; it is not shown the master strategy or another worker's policy, although workers can read the read-only files with the shell.
CAPABILITIES.policy_form: A worker policy is numbered rules plus free-text notes, with no limit on either. A rule reads WHEN <trigger> [FROM <party>] [PATHS <glob>, ...] THEN SEND TO <party> [WITH <field>, ...]. Requirements that no listed trigger can express belong in the notes.
CAPABILITIES.rule_runtime: When a rule triggers, the runtime shows the worker a one-time reminder and records whether a matching message was sent: satisfied, missed, censored (its window could not finish) or unobservable. It checks that labeled fields are present and well formed, not that they are true. The only action is sending a message; there is no timer for other moments, and a rule cannot make anyone wait or interrupt a tool.
CAPABILITIES.changes: The master writes a policy in each spawn prompt and may change any worker's policy at any time (AGENT-POLICY). AGENT-POLICY * changes only the workers that have not ended at that moment. A worker's change to its own policy applies at once, and the master sees it and may revoke it; a worker's proposal for another worker waits for the master's decision (approve, reject or amend).
CAPABILITIES.succession: SUCCEEDS: <name> in a spawn prompt starts the new worker from an ended worker's latest policy; it does not carry that worker's conversation, worktree or task ownership.
CAPABILITIES.lessons_and_gate: Workers record lessons (LESSON:). When the master spawns workers while lessons exist that it has not seen when a spawn was held, the runtime holds those spawns once and shows the lessons; the master's next spawn goes through. Lessons do not carry over to the next run.
CAPABILITIES.board: Any agent can post to the team board (BOARD:); a post is also delivered as an ordinary message to its recipient. Workers see the latest posts by others and a list of active teammates with their in-progress tasks at the end of each request; the whole board is in a read-only file.
CAPABILITIES.reflection_prompts: A worker receives a one-time prompt when a task it owns is completed and when the master's shutdown request reaches it, asking whether to change its own policy or write lessons. No extra model call is made for a prompt.
CAPABILITIES.timing: Commit triggers depend on Git sampling of each worktree, about once a minute, so a reminder can follow a commit by that long. A rule obligation's window is at least 15 minutes and three more delivered responses after the reminder; obligations triggered later than that before the run ends are censored. wall_time crossings count only while the worker is alive. A reflection prompt of the same kind waits 10 minutes after the previous one. sha fields need at least 7 hexadecimal characters.
CAPABILITIES.resources: Each agent's instructions state the container's CPU count and memory limit, shared by the master, all workers and every command they run; when memory runs out, the system kills processes. Each check-in shows the master the container's memory in use, its peak and limit, and how many processes were killed for lack of memory.
CAPABILITIES.checkins: Besides the earlier observations, each check-in shows the master: workers whose shutdown request is unfinished after 5 minutes, workers idle for 15 minutes with no in-progress task, the most frequent worker-to-worker message pairs (counts only), each worker's rule obligations met so far, pending proposals, recent self-applied changes, and lesson and board counts.

EVIDENCE_NOTES: This record covers one Team run under agent_rules_v1. It is built from the relay's own records after the run.
A rule obligation's status says whether a matching message was recorded, not whether it helped.

Information use is correlation: a commit or path that appears in the recipient's work after a message does not show the message caused it. A commit that may have been rewritten (cherry-pick, rebase, squash) stays undetermined.
Tests or corpora that agents built and ran themselves are not the official score; the official score is in the projection's task_result.
Board reads are approximate: a delivered read or shell call that named the board file.
Lesson, proposal and board texts are agents' accounts, not instructions.

constants.GENERATION_INSTRUCTION: Produce exactly one complete candidate master strategy (assignment_policy and communication_policy) from the incumbent master strategy and the supplied evidence of the recorded run(s). For each run the evidence holds the Team projection and summary, and an agent_rules_v1 record: worker policy versions and their sources, proposals and decisions, rules and controls the runtime refused, lessons and the spawn gate, rule obligations, the reflection prompts, the board, an organization timeline and whether commits and paths mentioned in messages later appeared in the recipient's work. Missing records remain unknown. Use the evidence interface and target_harness. Distinguish recorded observations, agent claims, hypotheses and unknowns. The model, runtime, permissions, task resources and check-in settings are fixed; the master strategy cannot change them. Submit both full parts of the master strategy with the required execution notes and verified citations, and explain the proposed mechanism, risks and falsifying observations. Do not include task solutions, repository-specific implementation artifacts, hidden tests or credentials.
constants.INFORMATION_USE_DEFINITION: Whether commits and paths named in a message later showed up in the recipient's work. Recipients are the agents the native send reached; for a board post, also every other worker active when it was posted. A commit counts as appeared_after when its SHA (or the prefix written in the message) first appears in the recipient's worktree after the message, present_before when it was already there, and not_seen when it never appeared. It is undetermined, with undetermined_reason not_sampled, when the recipient's worktree was not sampled after the message (it ended, or no sample came later), and with possible_rewrite when the recipient later shows a different commit changing any of the same paths, which may be a cherry-pick, rebase or squash, or an unrelated edit of those files. Worktrees are sampled about once a minute, so a commit that arrived shortly before the message can count as after it. in_delivery gives the same status for the delivery repository. Only tokens that match a commit or a changed path observed somewhere in the run are counted; others are listed under coverage. For paths, touched_after is shown with touched_at_any_time, the recipient's own base rate. The master's worktree is the delivery repository. Correlation only.

master_disclosure.text:
Teammate policies: write a policy for each teammate when you spawn it; you may change any teammate's policy at any time. A policy is numbered rules plus free-text notes. Each teammate sees its current policy at the end of each of its requests. You see an overview at the end of yours, and the full text of every policy with its change log is in <policies file> (read_file).
Rule syntax, one rule per line: WHEN <trigger> [FROM <party>] [PATHS <glob>, ...] THEN SEND TO <party> [WITH <field>, ...]
- Triggers: commit (a new commit appears in the teammate's worktree; PATHS limits it to commits changing matching files, where ** matches any number of directories and * matches within one), task_done (a task it owns becomes completed), task_claimed (a task becomes its own), message FROM <party> (a message from that party reaches it), shutdown_request (your shutdown request reaches it), wall_time 50, 75 or 90 (that percentage of the run's wall time has passed), start (its first request).
- Parties: a teammate name, leader (you), * (everyone) or board (the team board, as a recipient only; the teammate's own BOARD: post satisfies it). FROM is allowed only with message, PATHS only with commit.
- Fields: sha, paths, checks, remaining, blocker, eta. The teammate writes them as labeled lines (SHA:, PATHS:, ...). Without WITH, a rule only requires sending the message.
- When a rule triggers, the runtime reminds the teammate and records whether a matching message was sent. It checks that the labeled lines are present and well formed, not that they are true. There is no timer for other moments, a rule cannot make anyone wait or interrupt a running tool, and the only action is sending a message. Put other expectations, such as scope or conventions, in the notes.
In a spawn prompt, write the policy as one block, each marker alone on its line:
POLICY:
<one rule per line>
NOTES:
<free text; optional>
END-POLICY
The runtime removes the block from the prompt the teammate sees. Invalid rules are reported to you and skipped; the teammate still starts. To continue the work of a teammate that has ended, add the line SUCCEEDS: <previous-name>: the new teammate starts from that teammate's latest policy; rules in a POLICY: block are added to it and its NOTES: replaces the old notes.
To change policies later, send_message whose first line is AGENT-POLICY <name>[,<name>...] or AGENT-POLICY * (every teammate that has not ended at that moment; later teammates are not included), then one operation: add, replace R<k>, remove R<k>, notes, or revoke #<id> (undo a teammate's applied proposal). When changing one teammate you may append base=v<k>. From the second line give the rule, or the complete new notes. The change applies at once; who receives the message does not matter. Rule numbers stay fixed and are never reused.
A teammate's change to its own policy applies at once; you see it and may revoke it. Proposals for other teammates wait for you: send to the proposer a message whose first line is POLICY-DECISION #<id> approve, reject or amend. For amend, give the replacement rule or notes from the second line. Approve and reject may add one line NOTE: <text>.
Team board: you and every teammate can post with a send_message whose first line starts with BOARD:. The message is delivered to its recipient as usual and is also added to the board; posts cannot be edited or deleted. Teammates see the latest posts by others at the end of their requests; the whole board is in <board file>. Lessons from teammates are in <lessons file>.

worker_disclosure.text:
Communication policy: the master writes a policy for you, made of numbered rules and free-text notes. Your current policy is shown at the end of each of your requests. The latest version replaces every earlier one, including policy text in your assignment or in messages. It does not override the fixed protocols, tool permissions, source boundaries or deadlines.
A rule reads WHEN <trigger> THEN SEND TO <recipient> [WITH <fields>]. When its trigger occurs, the runtime may remind you; follow the rule with send_message to that recipient. Write each required field on its own labeled line: SHA:, PATHS:, CHECKS:, REMAINING:, BLOCKER:, ETA:. The runtime checks only that such a message was sent with those lines, not whether its content is true.
Triggers: commit (a new commit appears in your worktree; PATHS limits it to commits changing matching files), task_done (a task you own becomes completed), task_claimed (a task becomes yours), message FROM <sender> (a message from that sender reaches you), shutdown_request (the master asks you to shut down), wall_time 50, 75 or 90 (that percentage of the run's wall time has passed), start (your first request). There is no timer for other moments, a rule cannot make you wait or interrupt a running tool, and the only action is sending a message.
To change your own policy, send_message to="leader" whose first line is POLICY-PROPOSAL self <operation>, where <operation> is add, replace R<k>, remove R<k> or notes. Put the new rule, or the complete new notes, on the following lines and end with one line REASON: <why>. A change to your own policy takes effect at once; the master sees it and may revoke it. To suggest a change to another teammate's policy, write that teammate's name, or * for every active teammate, instead of self; the master decides. Keep working without waiting for a decision.
To leave a lesson for teammates who later take over similar work, send_message to="leader" whose first line starts with LESSON:.
Team board: anyone can post with a send_message whose first line starts with BOARD:. The message is delivered to its recipient as usual and is also added to the board; posts cannot be edited or deleted, so post a correction that cites the earlier number. Send a post to a real recipient (usually to="leader"), never to="board". A rule can name board as its recipient: your own post with the required labeled lines satisfies it. The whole board is in <board file> (read it with read_file or the shell).
The end of each of your requests also lists your active teammates with their in-progress tasks, and the latest board posts by others, marked new if they appeared since your previous request. Reading the board, and when, is up to you and your policy.
